findings.question: Q4
findings.title: R14-C-F2 is still open, though README section 9 marks it fixed. The entries listed just before a read-back (`before`) are thrown away unless an unread state is already recorded, so a spend state that rolls back in place during its own read-back is dropped and the executed action can be admitted and dispatched again
findings.evidence: owners.py:607 lists `before = self._entries(key)` for every handed account. On a successful read-back, `before` and `after` feed only `_seen_entries` (owners.py:740-743) and `_against_unread` (owners.py:744). `_against_unread` returns None straight away when no unread state is recorded (owners.py:674-676). So a read state whose `before` held a spend entry that `after` and the read history lack is accepted: `_seen` takes the read history (owners.py:739) and the listed spend is never recorded. On the not-read-back path, `_read_back` discards `before` and `_unread` lists the container again after the failed attempts (owners.py:613-618 -> 621-626). The recorded entries are therefore the container after any in-place rollback during those attempts, and if they are a prefix of `_seen_entries`, `_note_unread` records nothing (owners.py:656-659). The docstring at owners.py:590-591 says the entries are those held 'just before the read-back', and README:194-195 / owners.py:405 say 'held then'; neither is what the unread path records. README:625-626 lists 'Fixed, MINOR: R14-C-F2 / F14-F2 (a read state is checked against unread entries listed just before AND just after its read-back)', but R14-C-F2's own reproduction (review_r14_result.json, lens C) had no unread state ('diverged: [] unread: {}'). The round-14 control tests/mind/test_authority_review_r14.py:136-158 covers only the variant where the spend was first made unread by an earlier verification, which is F14-F2's case. The mutants list 'the after-read listing ignored' (README:399) but no mutant or control for R14-C-F2's no-unread case.
findings.reproduction: Static reading only; nothing was executed. Path 1 (R14-C-F2's recipe unchanged): on the battery fixture with BudgetReader.following(lambda: (dict(o.ledgers), dict(o.experiments))), the executor settles run.1 with a detail whose __str__, on the next verification's first read-back attempt, runs object.__setattr__(led, 'charges', s0.charges + (other.1,)) and raises the interpreter's 'changed size during iteration'. Attempt 2 reads S0+other.1. before=(spent, run.1) and after=(spent, other.1); no unread state is recorded, so owners.py:675-676 returns None, the record is accepted, and a fresh project_world + gateway.admit + dispatch of simulate_pulse runs the executor a second time. Path 2 (unread path): the same rollback goes to the observed tuple `earlier` (identical objects), and the account's to_dict override keeps raising the mutation error on all three attempts. `_unread` lists `earlier`, which `_seen_entries` extends, so nothing is recorded. After the override is removed, gateway.dispatch(admitted) re-admits on a history equal to `_seen` and the executor runs twice.
findings.why: The handed state (spent, run.1) was observed (its entry objects were listed), and the reader still decides on a state that does not begin with them. That contradicts README:226-228 ('a return to an earlier state never re-authorizes what such a state had moved past') and 196-199. The trigger bypasses the owner's BudgetHistoryViolation guard (object.__setattr__) or mutates the private _evaluations list, so under the trust-boundary rule it stays MINOR, as round 14 rated it. It is still a genuine correctness defect of the forward-only follower, so it keeps Q4 PARTIAL. The report's 'Fixed' disposition matters for the gate: it would let a later round treat Q4 as clean while the finding's own reproduction still holds.
findings.fix: Record `before` itself as the observed entries of the handed state. On a read state where `after` does not extend `before` (an in-place rollback during the read-back), do not accept the record: treat it as not read back with `before` passed to _note_unread, as R14-C-F2's fix proposed. On the not-read-back path, pass `before` (not a fresh listing) to _note_unread, and refuse for good when the fresh listing is not an extension of `before`. Add a control for R14-C-F2's no-unread scenario, plus a mutant that drops it, and correct the README section 9 disposition.

findings.question: Q4
findings.title: New in 7b4a0de8: an honest account that moved forward in place past a recorded unread state during a concurrent read-back is refused for good with the false reason 'rewrote the entries', contrary to README:240-241
findings.evidence: owners.py:681-686: a read state is cleared only if BOTH `before` and `after` extend the unread entries U, and is 'behind unread' only if U extends BOTH. Any other case goes to `_rewrote_unread`, and owners.py:748-750 records it in `_diverged` (for good). When before is a strict prefix of U and U is a strict prefix of after (all the same objects, an append-only move), neither test holds, so the account is refused for good with the text at owners.py:690-692 ('rewrote the entries of a state ... no longer begins with exactly those entry objects'), which is false. At 1c9fdd84 only `before` was compared (review_r14_result.json R14-C-F2 evidence: '`before` is used only to compare against a previously recorded unread state'), and this case was 'behind' (refused only while behind). README:240-241 says 'Concurrent verifications never refuse for good an account that only moved forward in place and that its owner reads back.' U is listed AFTER the other verification's failed attempts (owners.py:614, 621-622), so it can fall strictly between a concurrent verification's two listings. README section 8 (lines 497-513) documents honest torn read-backs of a large experiment that is extended every 0.1 s while one read-back takes about 0.45 s.
findings.reproduction: Static reading only; nothing was executed. Use a BOUND experiment extended in place at about 0.1 s intervals with a read-back of about 0.45 s. V1's three attempts tear (not read back) and `_unread` lists U with n+2 entries; it holds new entries, so it is recorded, and V1 compares. Meanwhile V2 listed before (n entries), succeeded on one attempt, and listed after (n+4 entries); it compares after V1. owners.py:681 fails (before is shorter than U), owners.py:684 fails (after is longer than U), and owners.py:686 + 748-750 refuse the account for good. Every later admission that binds it is refused until a new reader is built.
findings.why: A follower that refuses an honest forward-only account for good, saying it rewrote its history, asserts a false fact about the owner's account (a refusal reason that misstates why). It contradicts a stated guarantee and is a regression introduced by the round-14 change. It fails closed (no wrong admission), so it is MINOR, but it is a semantic defect of the budget follower and adds to Q4 PARTIAL.
findings.fix: When before, U and after form one identity-prefix chain (before ⊆ after, and each prefix-comparable with U), refuse to this verification only (behind / moved), never for good. Keep 'rewrote' for a container that is not prefix-comparable with U. Add a deterministic control that schedules U between the two listings.

findings.question: Q4
findings.title: New in 7b4a0de8: the seal fires on ANY BaseException raised while a handing is parsed, including the caller's own stack exhaustion or an asynchronous KeyboardInterrupt. It retires every account of the reader for good with the reason 'not a pair of account dicts'
findings.evidence: owners.py:872-882: `except BaseException as exc:` around `BudgetReader._handed(...)` sets `self._sealed = 'the execution side handed over what is not a pair of account dicts (<type>) ...'` for any exception class. owners.py:856-857 then refuses every later pin. `_handed` (owners.py:816-845) runs `cls(owner_id=...)`, `_items`, `text()` and the unpacking, a few frames below the `_follow()` call that has already succeeded. A RecursionError from a deep caller stack (the round-12 b1203 window, documented as 'the caller's own stack exhausted inside the reader'), a MemoryError, or an operator's Ctrl-C arriving inside `_handed` seals an honestly handed pair of dicts. README:208-209 says 'a verification's own deep call stack never refuses an honest account for good'. README:159-161 and owners.py:381-383 describe the seal as applying to 'a handing that is not a pair of dicts'. At 13051154 only the TypeError from `_items` was converted (CRIT14-1 evidence).
findings.reproduction: Static reading only; nothing was executed. Call gateway.admit through a desk whose budget reader follows plain dicts, from a call depth where `accounts()` still returns but `_handed`'s constructor frames overflow (the b1203 headroom window). `_sealed` is set with '(RecursionError)', and every later admission binding any account of that reader is OWNER_UNAVAILABLE from then on, although what was handed was a valid pair of dicts.
findings.why: This is a fail-closed availability regression, and the refusal reason misstates why ('not a pair of account dicts' for a stack or interrupt condition). It contradicts the README's claim about deep stacks. MINOR, but a semantic defect of the budget follower (Q4).
findings.fix: Seal only on the structural refusal (`_items`' TypeError, or a handed value that is not a 2-item pair). Treat RecursionError, MemoryError and interrupts in `_handed` as this verification leaving after being handed (`_leave(ticket, True)`), which is the documented residual. Alternatively, state the wider seal and its reason exactly in README section 4 and the docstring.

findings.question: Q4
findings.title: The round-14 seal (CRIT14-1's fix) is checked only when a pin starts. A verification already in flight when another verification seals the reader still compares after the seal, decides on a restored checkpoint, and the same admitted action is dispatched again.
findings.evidence: src/engcore/mind/world/owners.py:856-857: `if self._sealed is not None: raise` runs only at the top of pinned(), before the ticket is taken. owners.py:872-882: the seal is set when _handed raises, and that verification leaves through the finally at 889-894. _leave (owners.py:799-808) flags only verifications that are already waiting on it. _observe_all (owners.py:705-786) never reads self._sealed under the lock, so a verification that compares later has no pending ticket for the sealed one and decides on whatever it was handed. README section 4 (lines 159-161 and 239-240) and section 9 (round-14 dispositions: 'makes the reader refuse every account from then on') claim the opposite. Probe ~/br11-review/r15/A-scientific-authority/p1_seal_race.py (helpers in common.py; script C:\Users\DEV_KA~1\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-dev-kaeem-Downloads-Compressed-phyx\b5e3066d-77b7-465b-b1bf-cfd7098cdf27\scratchpad\r15\A-scientific-authority\p1.sh). Output ~/br11-review/r15/A-scientific-authority/p1.out at 95f3869e (owners imported from ~/forge-r15-review/src): proxy mode: 'VB read refused: the execution side handed over what is not a pair of account dicts', 'sealed: True', then 'VA (the same admitted action, dispatch started before the seal): [DISPATCHED AGAIN]' and 'executor calls: 2'. Control in the same probe (the same timeline with the spend handed in a dict and not read back): VA REFUSED, calls 1. Candidate fix, tested in a private archive copy: in _observe_all, refuse every key once _sealed is set, under the lock. With it the race is REFUSED with calls 1 (~/br11-review/r15/A-scientific-authority/p1_fixed.out), and test_authority_review_r13.py plus r14.py pass (27 passed).
findings.reproduction:
Battery fixture. BudgetReader.following(accounts): accounts() returns dict(o.ledgers), except a MappingProxyType once a flag is set, and it blocks on thread 'VA' until released. Admit simulate_pulse (r.admitted) at checkpoint F. Then:
1. Dispatch r.admitted. The executor settles run.1 and sets the proxy flag.
2. Start thread VA, which calls gateway.dispatch(r.admitted) again. Its pin takes its ticket and blocks inside accounts().
3. On the main thread, reader.read(BUDGET_LEDGER, solver) is handed the spend in a MappingProxyType, so the reader seals and refuses.
4. Restore o.ledgers[solver] = BudgetLedger.from_dict(F) and clear the flag.
5. Release VA. Its accounts() returns the restored F, which equals the observed history. No verification is pending, so it is accepted and the executor runs a second time (calls=2).
Command: wsl.exe -d Ubuntu-24.04 -- bash -s < .../scratchpad/r15/A-scientific-authority/p1.sh
findings.why: Q4's forward-only guarantee says no unobserved spend may lead to a duplicate dispatch. The seal exists because a non-dict handing 'may hold a spend' (CRIT14-1). Here exactly such a handing held the spend, the reader sealed, and a verification deciding after the seal still re-authorized the checkpoint the account had moved past, so the executor ran twice. The behaviour is new in 7b4a0de8 and not pre-accepted (the seal is listed as NOT pre-accepted). The README states 'from then on', and that is false for every verification already in flight. The equivalent dict handing (the control) is refused because _note_unread is consulted under the lock. The seal has no such check, so CRIT14-1 is closed only for sequential verifications.
findings.fix: In _observe_all, under self._changed, check self._sealed before deciding: if set, refuse every handed key to this verification, and also re-check it after the wait. Add a concurrent control alongside test_a_spend_handed_in_a_mapping_that_is_not_a_dict_is_never_redispatched that holds a verification in flight across the seal and asserts executor calls == 1. Add a mutant that drops the check.

findings.title: The round-14 seal (CRIT14-1 fix) is checked only when pinned() starts: a verification already past that check when another one is handed a non-dict mapping still compares and decides after the seal, so the executed action is dispatched again after a restore
findings.evidence: src/engcore/mind/world/owners.py:856-857 is the only read of self._sealed (`if self._sealed is not None: raise OwnerUnavailable(self._sealed)`), and it runs before the ticket is taken. The seal is set at 874-882. _observe_all (694-786) never looks at _sealed, neither in the first comparison nor in the re-check after the wait (775-783). The only thing that stops an in-flight verification is _leave(ticket, handed=True) (799-808), and that marks only verifications ALREADY WAITING for the sealing ticket. A verification that compares after the sealing one has left therefore decides normally. README section 4 lines 159-161 and 239-240 ('as is every account of a reader once it was handed something that is not a pair of dicts'), the seal's own text ('refuses every account from then on') and the tests/mind/test_authority_review_r14.py module docstring (lines 1-11) all claim the opposite. Probe: C:\Users\DEV_KA~1\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-dev-kaeem-Downloads-Compressed-phyx\b5e3066d-77b7-465b-b1bf-cfd7098cdf27\scratchpad\r15\F-round14-rewrites-deep\p1_seal_race.py, run in WSL as ~/br11-review/r15/F-round14-rewrites-deep/p1_seal_race.py against ~/forge-r15-review at 95f3869e; output in p1_seal_race.txt: '[redispatch] BAD: refused: the execution side handed over what is not a pair of account dicts (TypeError)...', 'sealed: True', 'GOOD (started before the seal, handed S0 after it): DISPATCHED AGAIN', 'executor calls = 2'. Control in the same run: a verification started after GOOD is refused with the seal text. '[record] ... AdmissionRecord.of ACCEPTED the original admission (S0) after the seal'.
findings.reproduction: Battery fixture, BudgetReader.following(accounts), ExecutionDesk(...).gateway(). accounts() returns a types.MappingProxyType for ledgers on thread 'BAD' and blocks on thread 'GOOD' until released. (1) Admit simulate_pulse on S0 and dispatch it: the executor settles run.1, giving S1, which is never read back. (2) Thread GOOD calls gateway.dispatch(r.admitted). It passes the seal check and blocks inside accounts(). (3) Thread BAD calls reader.pinned(). It is handed S1 in the proxy, seals the reader and leaves. (4) Restore checkpoint S0 by object replacement (o.ledgers[lid] = BudgetLedger.from_dict(s0)). (5) Release GOOD. It is handed S0 as a dict and reads it back. S0 equals the observed history, so it is accepted (no other verification is in flight), and the executor runs a second time. Each step is ordered by threading.Event, with no timing luck.
findings.why: A verification was handed the state that holds the action's spend. The reader then accepted a state without that spend and re-authorized the executed action, which is the Q4 forward-only guarantee (no unobserved spend leading to duplicate dispatch). This is the same outcome as CRIT14-1, which round 14 treated as MAJOR and which the seal was added to close. The seal closes it only for verifications that start after it, so the newest change left the MAJOR reachable through ordinary concurrency on one desk (the desk is documented to serve concurrent admissions). The report's claim that such a reader 'refuses every account from then on' is materially false. It is not the accepted 'left uncompared, only waiters refuse' residual, because the round-14 design explicitly promises more than that for a non-dict handing.
findings.fix: Check self._sealed under self._lock inside _observe_all: in the first comparison, refusing every account for that verification, and again in the post-wait re-check. Also record the seal before the sealing ticket leaves the in-flight set, so that any verification comparing after it sees the seal. Add a deterministic two-thread control (the p1 interleaving) that asserts executor calls == 1.

A read during which an honest settle lands in place (before n, after n+1) therefore leaves no known content. _note_unread (655-659) then records the next unread state even though it holds no new entry (its content was read). The same happens after an object-replacing resume that no verification has read yet, because the new entry objects are not a prefix of the old ones. A second unchanged resume is then 'rewrote' and goes into _diverged (681-686, 748-751). README section 4 lines 201-203 claims the opposite. True; executor calls 2`. ~/br11-review/r15/B-architecture/p2b_before_listing_dropped.py: a readable spend rolled back in place inside the next verification's read-back, with no unread record: `[rollback_in_readback] same authorization dispatched again: True; executor calls 2`.

Rated MINOR because every trigger needs execution-side tampering with its own owner object: an instance to_dict override, or object.__setattr__ past BudgetLedger's settle-only guard. The refutation attempt failed; the finding holds as stated.

Code at 95f3869e (src/engcore/mind/world/owners.py):
- pinned() reads `self._sealed` once, at lines 856-857, before the ticket and before `self._follow()`.
- The seal is set at lines 874-882, with the text 'this reader refuses every account from then on'.
- `_observe_all` (lines 694-786) never reads `_sealed`, neither at the comparison under `self._changed` nor in the post-wait recheck at lines 775-783.

No unread entries were recorded, because the sealing handing never reached `_read_back`/`_note_unread`. `pending` is empty because V2 left through `_leave` before V1 compared, and V1 was not in `_waiters`, so the 'left without comparing' flag does not reach it. V1 accepts D0 and the gateway re-executes the admitted action.

Refutation angles I tried:
(a) Is this just the accepted residual 'a spend and its rollback both between two verifications look like no change'? restore_only shows that residual yields the same outcome when nobody was handed S1. Here a verification WAS handed S1 and the reader explicitly sealed for that reason. Rounds 13-14 (R14-A-F1 et al., CRIT14-1) treated a handed-but-not-read-back state as one that must not be re-authorized. The noseal control proves the same interleaving is refused when S1 is handed as dicts.
